module_title: SAMR Model, TPACK Framework & NEP 2020 Digital Mandates
introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced KVS exams, this level explores the theoretical frameworks used to evaluate ICT integration (SAMR and TPACK) and critically aligns them with NEP 2020's vision for digital equity and blended learning.

core_concepts.title: The SAMR Model (Ruben Puentedura)
core_concepts.description:
A highly tested framework that assesses the depth of technology integration in a classroom. It has 4 progressive levels:
1. Substitution: Tech acts as a direct tool substitute with no functional change. (e.g., Typing an essay on MS Word instead of writing it on paper).
2. Augmentation: Tech acts as a direct substitute with functional improvement. (e.g., Typing the essay on MS Word and using the built-in Spell Check/Thesaurus).
3. Modification: Tech allows for significant task redesign. (e.g., Writing the essay on Google Docs so peers can live-edit and comment simultaneously).
4. Redefinition: Tech allows for the creation of new tasks that were previously inconceivable. (e.g., Turning the essay into a multimedia documentary and publishing it globally on a digital forum).

core_concepts.title: TPACK Framework (Mishra & Koehler)
core_concepts.description:
Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) identifies the three types of knowledge a teacher needs to successfully integrate ICT:
1. Content Knowledge (CK): What are you teaching? (e.g., The laws of physics).
2. Pedagogical Knowledge (PK): How do you teach? (e.g., Using constructivist 5E inquiry).
3. Technological Knowledge (TK): What digital tools are you using? (e.g., A PhET interactive simulation).
True 21st-century teaching happens at the intersection of all three (TPACK), where the teacher uses the right technology to enhance the pedagogy of specific content.

core_concepts.title: NEP 2020: Blended Learning and the Digital Divide
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 strongly advocates for Blended Learning to ensure resilience against future pandemics and to increase Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER). 
- Digital Divide Mitigation: Acknowledging that rural areas lack devices, NEP mandates the expansion of SWAYAM PRABHA (TV), Community Radio, and DIKSHA offline modes.
- Optimal Blended Ratio: The UGC issued guidelines post-NEP suggesting that Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) can teach up to **40% of any course syllabus online** (via SWAYAM) and 60% offline, officially mainstreaming the blended model.

important_entities.name: Enhancement vs. Transformation (SAMR)
important_entities.key_fact: The dividing line in the SAMR model.
important_entities.description: Substitution and Augmentation are considered 'Enhancement' steps (they make traditional teaching slightly better). Modification and Redefinition are 'Transformation' steps (they completely revolutionize the nature of the learning task). NCF 2023 pushes teachers to aim for Transformation.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common distractor in pedagogy exams is that 'Technology always improves learning.' TPACK explicitly argues against this. If a teacher uses an advanced VR headset (High TK) but teaches fact-memorization (Poor PK) of irrelevant facts (Poor CK), the technology is useless. Technology must serve pedagogy, not replace it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: CK = **What** you teach. PK = **How** you teach. TK = **With what** tool you teach.

exam_strategy_tips: If an advanced UGC NET question asks 'A teacher replaces a printed map with a digital map on a smartboard. According to the SAMR model, what level is this?', the answer is **Substitution**, because there is absolutely no functional change to the pedagogical task.
